rubric.criterion: Normal adopted embedding reaches a default ureq request carrying x-goog-api-key.
The inspected redirect implementation is the dependency version pinned by the repository.
Default ureq requests automatically follow Location values that can change origin or scheme.
rubric.evidence: Resolved ureq 2.12.1 agent.rs:251-266 defaults redirects to 5; unit.rs:154-187 joins Location without an origin restriction.

rubric.criterion: Redirect reconstruction retains the custom Gemini key header.
rubric.evidence: Resolved ureq 2.12.1 unit.rs:216-235 removes only content-length, cookie, and authorization; x-goog-api-key survives.

rubric.criterion: KCS has no later origin/scheme comparison before the redirected send.
rubric.evidence: gemini_embedding.rs:120-148 delegates the request entirely to top-level ureq and contains no redirect callback or target validation.

evidence: crates/kcs-adapter/src/gemini_embedding.rs:71-80 resolves the secret and lines 120-148 attach it as x-goog-api-key.
Resolved ureq 2.12.1 lib.rs:512-519,580-583 constructs a default AgentBuilder for top-level post.
Resolved ureq 2.12.1 agent.rs:251-266 enables five redirects by default.
Resolved ureq 2.12.1 unit.rs:154-235 accepts cross-origin Location, converts POST 301/302/303 to GET, reuses headers, and fails to strip x-goog-api-key.
counterevidence: An accepted origin must return a cross-origin 301, 302, or 303; no open redirect at Google's default endpoint was established.
A deliberately malicious configured first origin already receives the key, so the incremental issue requires a trusted, compromised, misconfigured, or intermediary-controlled accepted origin.
HTTPS protects the initial response against an ordinary on-path redirect injection.
POST bodies are emptied on 301/302/303 and body-bearing POST 307/308 responses are not followed, so this candidate proves key disclosure rather than embedding-text forwarding.
Valid credentials, adapter opt-in, and operator-driven embedding remain required.
proof_gap: No two-listener loopback capture was run and default Google redirect behavior was not established. The V10 locked-dependency header-retention trace is complete.
remediation_subsumption_decision: Disable automatic redirects for credentialed Gemini requests or implement a redirect loop that permits only explicitly approved same-origin, non-downgrade targets and reconstructs credentials after validation. Generic destination binding from CAND-026 does not by itself control library-internal redirects.

attack_steps: An operator performs an approved embedding operation using a valid Gemini credential.
KCS sends the request with the credential in x-goog-api-key through the default ureq 2.12.1 agent.
The accepted origin returns a 301, 302, or 303 with a cross-origin or downgraded Location.
ureq rewrites the POST to a bodyless GET, strips standard Authorization/Cookie headers but retains x-goog-api-key, and sends that credential to the redirect origin.
assumptions: The initially approved HTTPS origin is trusted enough to receive the key but may be compromised, misconfigured, or redirect through a lower-trust origin.
The redirected origin can observe the custom API-key header.
A cross-origin 301/302/303 occurs; this behavior was not established for the default Google endpoint.
attack_path_facts.context: Normal adopted embedding execution reaches a remote-response trust boundary. The configured service identity is an operator choice, but redirect destinations are remote-controlled and are not rebound to that approved identity.
attack_path_facts.in_scope: yes; credential-origin and redirect-destination binding are explicit I3 security properties
attack_path_facts.exposure: outbound authenticated adapter request with a remote-controlled redirect response; no KCS listener exists
attack_path_facts.identity: The approved Gemini service or an accepted intermediary controls the redirect response; the unauthorized redirect origin receives the reusable API credential.
attack_path_facts.cross_boundary: yes: x-goog-api-key crosses from the approved provider origin to a second, unapproved origin
preconditions: Valid Gemini credential and per-adapter network opt-in
The accepted origin returns a cross-origin 301, 302, or 303
The redirect target is observable by a lower-trust recipient
attack_path_facts.attacker_control: yes over the redirect target when the accepted origin, compromised service, or relevant intermediary can emit the response; no default-endpoint open redirect was proven
mitigations: HTTPS authenticates the initial origin against ordinary on-path response injection.
Per-adapter opt-in and a valid credential are required.
The embedding body is discarded on 301/302/303, so this path proves credential rather than text disclosure.
Body-bearing 307/308 POST responses are not automatically followed by this exact path.
ureq removes standard Authorization and Cookie headers, but not x-goog-api-key.
attack_path_facts.target_reach: one Gemini credential and each embedding request encountering a qualifying redirect
secrets_references: x-goog-api-key request header retained across redirect
counterevidence: No open redirect or cross-origin redirect was established at Google's default endpoint.
A malicious custom base already receives the key on the initial request.
HTTPS blocks an ordinary on-path attacker from injecting the first redirect.
The request body is not forwarded on the proven 301/302/303 route.
blindspots: No two-origin loopback capture was run.
The frequency and destination behavior of real accepted-origin redirects are unknown.
controls: Disable redirects for credential-bearing requests or enforce same-origin and no-scheme-downgrade redirect policy.
Strip all provider credential headers before any origin change.
attack_path_facts.confidence: high (0.96) for header retention; medium for real-world redirect occurrence
attack_path_facts.rationale: A remote in-scope actor can cause a reusable credential to cross an approved origin boundary. The missing evidence that the default endpoint actually issues such a redirect constrains likelihood to medium. The mandatory matrix maps high impact and medium likelihood to medium.
